def-nrqmx-bloch-fiber-model: The Definition specifies finite-range shifts, the Fourier transform and a nonempty band cluster; it does not characterize a property by equivalent conditions.
lem-nrqmx-bloch-fiber-model-properties: The argument bounds the shift sum, extends the Fourier isometry, and constructs smooth gapped Riesz projectors; no converse to these conclusions is claimed.
def-nrqmx-determinant-line-projector: The Definition forms the top exterior power of a positive-rank range bundle and names its projector; it asserts no equivalence between predicates.
lem-nrqmx-determinant-line-projector-wel: The argument uses polynomial minors and wedge functoriality to show that the exterior projector is smooth, Hermitian, idempotent and rank one, without a reverse implication.
lem-nrqmx-determinant-curvature-is-trace: The calculation differentiates the top wedge frame and cancels off-diagonal one-form pairs to obtain trace curvature; this identity is not an iff criterion.
lem-nrqmx-degree-area-formula: The proof normalizes the sphere area and applies naturality of the homology pairing to compute the degree integral; it states an equality, not an equivalence of properties.
thm-nrqmx-bloch-projector-chern: The determinant-line reduction gives integrality, continuity gives homotopy invariance, and Stokes gives zero Chern number from a global frame; no converse frame-existence assertion is made.
thm-nrqmx-two-band-degree-formula: The Pauli trace calculation computes the upper and lower Chern numbers from the sphere degree under a nowhere-zero d vector; it does not characterize when a general projector has that degree.
thm-nrqmx-finite-band-adiabatic-velocity: Euler–Lagrange differentiation of the explicitly adopted single-band action yields the velocity equations; it neither proves a converse variational claim nor a quantum approximation error.
ex-nrqmx-two-band-gap-closures: The four sine-zero momenta in verification1.1 establish both directions of gap closure precisely at the three mass values; the degree table follows by signed regular preimages.
cex-nrqmx-smooth-frame-obstruction: The lower band at mass one has Chern number minus one; a global periodic frame would force zero, giving one counterexample to a universal frame assertion rather than an iff theorem.
lem-nrqmx-scaled-plancherel: The proof composes the explicitly invertible frequency dilation with Plancherel and uses Schwartz density for uniqueness; the claim is unitary extension, not a characterization with a reverse direction.
lem-nrqmx-weyl-hilbert-schmidt-bound: The midpoint/difference change of variables computes the kernel norm by Plancherel; Cauchy–Schwarz then bounds the induced integral operator, without any converse norm criterion.
thm-nrqmx-wigner-marginals: The proof establishes Weyl pairing, reality and two marginals by Fourier inversion and Fubini and exhibits a negative first-excited state; these are direct identities and a counterexample, not equivalent predicates.
lem-nrqmx-bounded-symbol-estimate: The packet resolution, cross-packet integration by parts and Schur estimate bound the Weyl form, after which Riesz represents it; there is no converse claiming bounded operators force the symbol derivative assumptions.
thm-nrqmx-schwartz-moyal-remainder: The Weyl translation product and exponential Taylor formula construct a Schwartz remainder and bound its Schur kernel; the result is a direct composition identity with no converse hypotheses.
lem-nrqmx-cubic-moyal-commutator-remaind: The kinetic kernel is exact and the symmetric third-order potential Taylor remainder yields the bounded error symbol; the claim is an implication from the stated derivative bounds, not their necessity.
thm-nrqmx-quadratic-egorov: The graph-core commutator and transported compact symbol give a Duhamel comparison for fixed finite times; vanishing cubic potential remainder gives the quadratic special case, without a converse quadraticity criterion.
ex-nrqmx-gaussian-wigner-flow: The Hermite core check permits exact quadratic Egorov, and an orthogonal phase-space rotation transports the explicit Gaussian density; the example computes one model, not an equivalent-condition test.
cex-nrqmx-wigner-negative: The polynomial-Gaussian Wigner calculation yields a negative disk and refutes universal positivity; the top-level claim is this explicit counterexample, not a biconditional characterization of states.
def-nrqmx-scattering-channel-data: The Definition names the two separate strong wave limits, completeness and a conditional scattering composite; its finite-channel input is expressly additional, with no equivalence assertion to reverse.
def-nrqmx-resonance-matrix-element-poles: The Definition specifies resolvent test elements and a local pole order with nonvanishing factor; it neither asserts a continuation exists nor characterizes resonances as eigenvalues.
lem-nrqmx-gaussian-resolvent-continuatio: Polar integration, a Laplace integral and holomorphic identity continuation compute one Gaussian resolvent element near a positive energy; no converse continuation criterion is asserted.
thm-nrqmx-short-range-scattering-complet: The proof matches Fourier and stationary normalizations to the compact-support suppliers and deduces completeness and the positive-energy formula; it does not claim those conclusions require compact support.
thm-nrqmx-finite-channel-wigner-smith: Differentiating a unitary matrix proves Hermiticity and the determinant trace identity, then constant basis changes give conjugation; no converse condition or operational time equivalence is asserted.
thm-nrqmx-rank-one-resonance-continuatio: The continued rank-one quotient has an exact finite-order pole when its numerator is nonzero, and self-adjointness excludes a nonreal eigenvalue; only these sufficient conditional inputs are claimed.
cex-nrqmx-cook-not-completeness: The explicit embedding into the first of two absolutely continuous summands is an isometric wave limit with a proper range; this refutes a universal implication rather than asserting an iff characterization.
ex-nrqmx-single-phase-time-delay: Substituting a scalar unitary phase in the Wigner–Smith definition gives twice hbar times the phase derivative; the example makes no converse or measured-arrival-time assertion.
def-nrqmx-finite-hermitian-frame-and-gra: The Definition specifies a real Hermitian frame, its synthesis, Gram pseudoinverse and canonical dual; it names constructions rather than claiming two predicates equivalent.
alg-nrqmx-linear-tomography-procedure: The algorithm takes a spanning finite POVM and returns the canonical linear frequency combination; it makes no converse or universal positive-output claim.
lem-nrqmx-finite-hermitian-trace-inner-p: Trace cyclicity and Hermitian eigenvalues prove a real positive pairing; the Gram calculation identifies the synthesis kernel, but the top-level result is not an iff criterion.
lem-nrqmx-frame-pseudoinverse-reconstruc: The spectral Penrose formula and synthesis projection reconstruct every Hermitian matrix from a spanning family, including redundant frames; no converse spanning characterization is claimed.
lem-nrqmx-bernoulli-hoeffding: Finite product expectations and two exponential Markov bounds give the two-sided frequency tail, including endpoint Bernoulli laws; the tail inequality is not claimed equivalent to independence.
thm-nrqmx-tomography-identifiability-sta: Exact dual reconstruction and an induced norm bound are followed by a finite union of Bernoulli tails under the stipulated product law; no converse identifiability or independence theorem is asserted.
ex-nrqmx-pauli-tomography: The six displayed effects span the four real Hermitian qubit coordinates; their Gram eigenspaces produce the dual and an explicit nonpositive frequency output, not an iff claim.
thm-nrqmx-instrument-stinespring-registe: Finite Kraus labels construct an isometry and orthogonal outcome registers, and the partial trace recovers each map; this proves existence from the instrument hypotheses, without a reverse criterion.
thm-nrqmx-sharp-joint-measurability: Commuting products construct a joint POVM, while the support argument forces every joint effect to equal the corresponding projection product; both directions and uniqueness are explicitly proved.
def-nrqmx-finite-channel-families: The Definition independently names the semigroup law and CP-divisibility as map properties; it does not assert these distinct conditions are equivalent.
def-nrqmx-finite-jump-trajectories: The Definition writes ordered finite jump products and their weights, includes the no-jump term and permits zero jump labels; it expressly leaves normalization to a theorem rather than stating an equivalence.
ex-nrqmx-finite-environment-recurrence: Two exact dephasing times erase and restore distinct qubit states, disproving both semigroup composition and divisibility for that family; no general equivalence between them is asserted.
ex-nrqmx-amplitude-damping-jump-law: The diagonal no-jump factor gives survival and the single jump gives an exponential density; zero rate leaves survival one. This is a model computation without an iff classification.
pthm-nrqmx-finite-reduction-channel: Environment matrix elements provide normalized Kraus operators and hence a channel; a separate two-qubit recurrence shows a family need not be semigroup or divisible. No converse is asserted.
pthm-nrqmx-amplitude-damping-model: The four matrix-unit generator powers sum to the stated population and coherence exponentials under the separately adopted GKSL model; this is a solution formula, not an equivalence of model assumptions.
pthm-nrqmx-jump-unravelling-finite: Variation of constants and a factorial remainder bound identify the normalized branch expansion, including no jump and zero rate family; the ensemble identity is not a converse microscopic trajectory characterization.
def-nrqmx-finite-mode-g2-statistic: The Definition divides the second factorial count moment by the positive finite mean squared for one assigned mode; it is a statistic definition without a biconditional about density operators.
pthm-nrqmx-jaynes-cummings-blocks: The conserved excitation blocks and their two-by-two characteristic polynomials give the splitting, and the squared-block domain gives self-adjointness for the chosen rotating-wave operator; no converse Hamiltonian classification is asserted.
pthm-nrqmx-beam-splitter-count-statistic: The passive creation-operator expansion gives the binomial count law and coherent product output, including vacuum and transmission endpoints; it does not characterize all processes with those statistics.
pthm-nrqmx-finite-mode-loss-channel: Vacuum embedding, unitary conjugation and partial trace give a CPTP map; number and coherent inputs plus endpoint isometries compute its action, without an iff criterion for arbitrary channels.
def-nrqmx-spin-half-tensor-chain: The Definition fixes the finite tensor chain, adjacent swaps and singlet operators, including an empty bond family at one site; these are explicit constructions with no converse property assertion.
def-nrqmx-planar-two-particle-configurat: The Definition removes the collision diagonal and takes the transposition quotient of two planar points; it makes no iff topological classification or particle-statistics claim.
def-nrqmx-planar-character-line-bundle: The Definition specifies the integer deck action with inverse character phase and names its quotient charts and monodromy convention; it does not assert an equivalence with a classification theorem.
thm-nrqmx-planar-character-line-bundle: Explicit interval sheets give the universal cover, character phases give flat charts, and lifted endpoints compute monodromy; the result establishes these constructions directly, not an iff classification of every flat line bundle.
lem-nrqmx-finite-symplectic-generator-fa: Positive mode count makes the matrices at least two-by-two, while rank reduction explicitly covers zero and full upper-left rank by omitting empty subblocks; no zero-mode space is included.
lem-nrqmx-finite-maslov-phase-parity: The hypothesis fixes at least one mode and an invertible upper-right generating chart; the phase comparison is between two nonempty endpoint propagator paths, not an empty mode or empty path family.
thm-nrqmx-finite-mode-bogoliubov: At least one mode is assumed, but the vacuum and zero creation-mixing matrix are allowed; the finite CCR computation and transformed-vacuum norm contain all such zero terms.
lem-nrqmx-williamson-normal-form: There is at least one symplectic two-dimensional block because the mode count is positive; the induction permits an empty remaining complement only at its terminal step and imposes no spectrum simplicity.
thm-nrqmx-gaussian-covariance-uncertaint: The product of thermal factors has a positive finite number of modes; every factor has trace one, including the vacuum endpoint, and the state spectral expansion cannot be empty for trace one.
lem-nrqmx-finite-mode-fock-schr-identifi: Positive mode count fixes a nonempty product index, while total occupation zero is explicitly the vacuum sector in the sector basis calculation; no zero-mode identification is claimed.
lem-nrqmx-finite-symplectic-implementers: The Weyl family is indexed by all real labels including the zero label; positive finite mode count and positive hbar exclude the zero-dimensional representation, while the identity label is included.
lem-nrqmx-schwartz-joint-quadrature-grap: The graph norm contains exactly the positive finite number of coordinate multiplication and derivative pairs; zero vectors are admitted and cutoff/mollified approximation applies to them as well.
thm-nrqmx-free-laplacian-form-domain: The form sum has precisely three fixed derivative coordinates, not an arbitrary potentially empty family; the zero Sobolev vector gives zero form and Fourier multiplier in the proof.
lem-nrqmx-projector-bundle-kato-well-def: If the base is empty, range-bundle assertions are vacuous and no path from the nonempty interval exists; positive-base local frames and the Kato solution are constructed wherever a point or path is supplied.
lem-nrqmx-c2-projector-chern-integrality: The normalization divides by the fixed nonzero real constant two times pi; the contour radius is one half and the inverse comparison bound is strictly below one, so no vanishing denominator parameter is suppressed.
thm-nrqmx-adiabatic-geometric-phase-boun: The matrix family is indexed on the fixed nonempty interval from zero to one; an empty spectral cluster gives the zero projector and trivial leakage if permitted, while the rank-one factorization is expressly conditional.
def-nrqmx-magnetic-form-data: The covariant derivative sum has the fixed index set from one to positive dimension; the zero test function is allowed and all local integrals are finite by compact support and locally integrable potential.
lem-nrqmx-landau-form-diagonalization: Oscillator indices are all nonnegative integers, including the ground index; the zero coefficient family is allowed and every series term then vanishes. Nonzero charge-field product is a separate translation hypothesis.
lem-nrqmx-landau-3d-form-diagonalization: The transverse oscillator sum includes its ground mode and the momentum plane is fixed; all coefficients may vanish, giving the zero vector and zero weighted form. No arbitrary empty index family is selected.
pthm-nrqmx-landau-direct-integral: The oscillator family is indexed by every real momentum and every nonnegative level, including the ground level, with all-zero coefficients permitted; nonzero magnetic coupling ensures positive oscillator frequency.
pthm-nrqmx-pauli-square-identity: The displayed kinetic and spin sums run over exactly three fixed coordinates; the zero compactly supported spinor gives both sides zero, and there is no variable empty family of fields.
thm-nrqmx-floquet-galerkin-correctness: The harmonic index sets have sizes two times bandwidth plus one and two times cutoff plus one; even bandwidth or cutoff zero retains the central harmonic, so the block assignment family is never empty.
thm-nrqmx-ritz-upper-bounds: The Statement explicitly assigns positive infinity to an empty k-plane variational family and to the empty essential-spectrum threshold; each claimed Ritz value instead requires trial-space dimension at least k.
